recognize_zh: 周邊血液中兩顆中型淋巴球，細胞質深藍、無顆粒且有細胞質突起（cytoplasmic bleb），細胞核略不規則並可見小核仁，是 T 細胞前淋巴球性白血病（T-PLL）的典型細胞外觀。
features: Medium-sized lymphoid cells larger than normal small lymphocytes
Intensely basophilic agranular cytoplasm with a cytoplasmic protrusion (bleb)
Oval to slightly irregular nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin
Small but visible nucleolus in the larger cell
Background red cells with echinocytes (likely artifactual crenation)
describe_en: High-power view of the peripheral blood shows two medium-sized lymphoid cells with moderately condensed chromatin, slightly irregular oval nuclei and a small visible nucleolus in the larger cell. The cytoplasm is deeply basophilic, agranular and shows a characteristic cytoplasmic protrusion. The background red cells show crenation. Findings are consistent with T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia; flow cytometry (CD7 bright, CD4/CD8 pattern) and TCL1A/MTCP1 rearrangement studies are recommended.

ddx.vs: B-prolymphocytes have a more prominent central nucleolus and paler cytoplasm without blebs, and express B-cell markers rather than T-cell markers.
Sézary cells have cerebriform, grooved nuclei without nucleoli and usually CD7 negative, whereas T-PLL cells are CD7 bright with basophilic blebbed cytoplasm.
ATLL shows polylobated 'flower' nuclei, CD25 positivity and HTLV-1 serology.
Reactive lymphocytes are heterogeneous with abundant cytoplasm scalloping around red cells, not a monotonous population of blebbed basophilic cells.
